beats.say: Twenty five years passed between when initial designs for the James Webb Space Telescope began in 1996 and its launch.
That quarter of a century wait is longer than an entire generation of students growing up from nursery to university.
Construction was completed in 2016 following decades of careful engineering and development across the globe.
The enormous primary mirror consists of eighteen hexagonal mirror segments made of gold plated beryllium.
It is named after James E Webb who served as the administrator of NASA from 1961 to 1968.
A powerful rocket finally carried the incredible observatory into orbit on 25 December 2021, bringing us back to when

facts: The James Webb Space Telescope was launched on 25 December 2021 on an Ariane 5 rocket.
The telescope is named after James E Webb who was the administrator of NASA from 1961 to 1968.
The primary mirror consists of 18 hexagonal mirror segments made of gold plated beryllium.
Initial designs for the telescope began in 1996.
